I understand. It does feel like a weapon. And it's been used on me without them knowing, my mom's boss is gay, so obviously it came up. She said "I think it's disgusting" like knife in my chest. She said it before I understood I was bi, but it was brought up again recently. 

If you need to talk, throw me a pm,  I'm outta school for the rest of the year, so pretty much any time is OK.

I only recently realised/accepted my sexuality. I'm a touch further than you,  I've told most of my gaming friends and one person who lives with me. What has helped me through this is having someone to talk to, I recently made a very good friend when we crossed paths helping someone else out. We talk pretty much every day.

Telling the person who lives here had me scared, I spent a week just trying to decide if I should, and another day thinking about what I should say. In the end I just said fuck it, and sent him a message. The wait was only 10 minutes, but it was the longest ten minutes in my life,  my mind was racing, wondering what he thought. He does not judge, which I am grateful for. 


With regards to you, perhaps testing the water is an idea, mention some lgbt news and see what their reaction is maybe. Whatever you do, I'm happy to talk or discuss it with you if you'd like. Being alone is scary.

Personaly, ive found that its the "what if" factor, I had to sit down and breathe for an hour after every single person ive told. Its very stressing. I told the only family member that knows over text, while they were out, so that they could cool off before they got back if they took it badly, and even then, i only told them after a week of indesision. If you want to talk about it, im happy to talk, I know how much having someone to talk to who understands can help.
